title: Error Handling Basics
description: Learn how to handle errors gracefully in GraphQL with Hot Chocolate.

data.text: GraphQL has a built-in error model. Errors are returned alongside data, so clients can handle partial failures gracefully.
Hot Chocolate returns errors in the standard GraphQL error format with message, locations, path, and extensions.
Throw `GraphQLException` to return a clean error to the client. Hot Chocolate formats it automatically.

data.title: Throw GraphQLException
data.content: Throw an error when a book is not found.

data.text: Use `IExceptionFilter` to transform exceptions globally. This is useful for logging and returning consistent error codes.

data.title: Exception Filter

terms.definition: An exception that Hot Chocolate converts to a GraphQL error.
An interface for intercepting and transforming exceptions before they reach the client.
Additional metadata on an error, such as a code or classification.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: GraphQL returns errors alongside partial data
Error codes help clients react programmatically
data.takeaway: Next, we'll create custom exceptions for domain errors.
